clue.text: Avon's most popular performer

parts.note: read as a clue, a star (NOVA) that is turned round gives the letters of this river's name

explanation.surface: Who is the best-loved entertainer from Shakespeare's Avon?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: a nova is a kind of star, and turning NOVA round gives AVON, so the answer phrase read as wordplay produces the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the headline act, the performer the audience likes best.

clue.text: The masses listened to broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken out on air, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: Ordinary people tuned in to a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that HEARD is said aloud, giving the same sound as HERD.
explanation.definitionFit: The herd is a dismissive idiom for ordinary people acting as a crowd.

clue.text: Fish extracts

definitions.meaning: small silvery food fish of the salmon family
a verb: gets metal out of ore by heating

explanation.definitionFit: Smelts are small edible fish, and smelting is extracting metal from ore by melting it.

clue.text: Bomb is terrible danger to earth

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of danger are thrown into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: An explosive device poses an awful threat to the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DANGER into GRENAD, and E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small hand-thrown bomb.

clue.text: Republican with guile and extremely erudite wit

parts.note: art in the sense of cunning or trickery

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme ends, the first and last letters of erudite

explanation.surface: A clever, well-read Republican politician is admired for sharp humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'erudite', E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty reply in conversation, a form of wit.

clue.text: American statesman was nothing out of the ordinary

indicators.note: out of the ordinary suggests an unusual state, so the letters of nothing are reordered

explanation.surface: A US politician was entirely unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says he was nothing special, but 'out of the ordinary' is the anagram signal working on 'nothing' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first US president and a founding statesman.

clue.text: Predict Iran has uranium hidden in city

indicators.note: hidden in means the following letters are tucked inside the word for predict

parts.note: to bet is to stake money on a forecast
IR is the international code for Iran
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A forecast that Iran is concealing nuclear material somewhere urban.
explanation.walkthrough: The nuclear-secrets surface disguises a plain container: 'hidden in' tells the solver to tuck the Iran and uranium letters inside the betting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is a city, the capital of Lebanon.

clue.text: River boat without flag

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the boat word goes around the river letter

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered boat

explanation.surface: A river vessel sails with no flag flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: STEAMER wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant.

clue.text: Very happy to be told right away

indicators.note: away says a letter is sent off, here the one standing for right

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to hear news immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but means remove R: RELATED loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated is a synonym of overjoyed or thrilled.

clue.text: He takes out barmaids regularly

indicators.note: regularly asks for letters at a steady interval, here the first, third, fifth and seventh of barmaids

explanation.surface: A man habitually dates women who work behind the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks alternate letters of 'barmaids': B, R, A, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Brad is a man's name, so it can stand for a male 'he' in a clue.

clue.text: Hires canal barge in the northwest

indicators.note: barge suggests bumping and shoving, so the letters of the two words are pushed about

explanation.surface: Someone rents a narrowboat in the north west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge' rearranges HIRESCANAL; the canal holiday surface makes 'barge' read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a county in the north west of England, standing for the region loosely.

clue.text: Not quite the most boring American statesman

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a letter short of complete, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A US politician who was very nearly the dullest of them all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter, T, from DULLEST.
explanation.definitionFit: John Foster Dulles was US Secretary of State under Eisenhower.

clue.text: Menace dwelling in chamber

parts.note: to lower (or lour) is to look threatening or menacing

explanation.surface: A threat lurks in a room of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: LOWER here rhymes with 'flower' and means scowl threateningly, not 'drop'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower house is one chamber of a two-part parliament, such as the Commons.

clue.text: Some found Eton a terrific blast!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few pupils thought the famous school was tremendous fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English private school; the answer runs through 'founD ETON A Terrific'.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to blow up, to blast.

clue.text: Finally gives woman liquid nitrogen to make frozen sculpture

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word gives

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

indicators.note: liquid means flowing and unfixed, so the letters of woman run into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hands a lady some liquid nitrogen to produce an ice statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid nitrogen' reads as one phrase, but 'liquid' is the anagram signal for 'woman' while 'nitrogen' gives its own symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowman is a figure sculpted out of packed snow.

clue.text: The least active sportsmen

indicators.note: active suggests lively movement, so the letters of the two words are set moving

explanation.surface: Sporting types are the laziest people around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' rearranges THELEAST; the surface 'least active' is a joke since athletes are the most active.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes are people who compete in sports.

clue.text: Animal in distress bites nearly everybody

indicators.note: in distress means troubled and disordered, so the letters of bites are jumbled
nearly says the word stops one letter short

explanation.surface: A suffering creature snaps at almost everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' rearranges BITES into BESTI; 'nearly' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestial means animal-like, as in brutish animal instincts; both are adjectives here.

clue.text: Maybe Donald Rumsfeld would allow one to torture in camera?

indicators.note: to torture is to twist painfully, so the letters of the phrase are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A dig at the US defence chief who approved harsh interrogation behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torture' rearranges INCAMERA; 'in camera' means in private, a legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Rumsfeld, US Defense Secretary, is one example of a US citizen.

clue.text: We see it to be terrible humbug, perhaps

indicators.note: to be terrible suggests a mess, so the letters of the three words are scrambled

explanation.surface: We find it is awful nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be terrible' rearranges WESEEIT. A humbug is a striped British boiled mint, not just nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a boiled mint, an example of a sweet or sweetie.

clue.text: Perhaps Cherie starts to write lampoons and satirical verse

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement among others, so the letters are reordered
starts to picks the opening letters of write and lampoons

explanation.surface: Maybe the Prime Minister's wife is beginning to pen mocking rhymes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives W and L, added to CHERIE and rearranged under 'Perhaps'. Cherie Blair is the wife of former UK prime minister Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line verse about a named person.

clue.text: Stay in hostel in Germany

annotationWithheld.why: Stay in hostel in Germany (6): IN and GER account for INGER, but no word in the clue gives the opening L; no blog found to confirm the parse

clue.text: Colours for Mary Whitehouse?

definitions.meaning: a flag or standard carried as an emblem
a person who bans things, as the campaigner against TV sex and violence wanted

explanation.walkthrough: Mary Whitehouse was a British campaigner who demanded bans on sex and violence on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag, and a banner is also, playfully, someone who bans.

clue.text: Recovered gambler

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling better means recovered, and a better is one who bets.

clue.text: Unclear when it's essential to imprison pacifist

indicators.note: to imprison means the word for essential locks up the pacifist

parts.note: CO is a conscientious objector, one who refuses to fight

explanation.surface: It is muddled when locking up a peace campaigner is thought vital.
explanation.walkthrough: CO, short for conscientious objector, is the usual crossword pacifist; 'to imprison' puts it inside the word for essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoherent means muddled, not clearly expressed.

clue.text: No runs at all in match

definitions.meaning: in cricket, out for nought in both innings of a game

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who scores a duck (zero) in both innings 'bags a pair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two ducks in cricket, and a pair is also a match or set of two.

clue.text: Person serving king's son has maturity

annotationWithheld.why: Person serving king's son has maturity (4): AGE is maturity, but nothing in the clue gives the opening P, and the definition boundary is unclear; no blog found
annotationWithheld.clue: Person serving king's son has maturity

clue.text: Monster is seen at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters of the two words drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A sea creature has been sighted out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ISSEEN. Nessie is the nickname of the Loch Ness monster in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the popular name for the legendary Loch Ness monster.

clue.text: Magi rode out to find sign

indicators.note: out suggests something wrong or disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Wise Men ride off in search of a star to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MAGIRODE; the Nativity surface makes 'sign' look like the star.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideogram is a written symbol standing for an idea, a kind of sign.
